svg.text: µPD78C14GF mask-ROM reader — Raspberry Pi Pico 2 wiring
Port of devinacker/upd7811-reader. Pico 2 (RP2350) replaces the 27C256, 74HCT373, crystal and USB-UART. Chip pin numbers = 64-pin QFP (GF-3BE).
U2 74HCT04 (VCC pin 14 = +5 V, GND pin 7; tie unused inputs 11, 13 to GND)
Power and static connections on the µPD78C14
MODE links (this is the whole trick)
Both MODE pins are pulled HIGH at reset → 64 KB external-ROM boot from the Pico.
The reader code jumps to its 8000h mirror, then drives PC7 low → MODE0 = 0
→ internal mask ROM appears at 0000h–3FFFh while code keeps running at 8000h+.
Never wire the MODE pins straight to 5 V: they are also outputs (M1, IO/M) — use the pull-ups.
22 kΩ pull-up to +5 V on every unused input (or a 22 kΩ / 10 kΩ resistor network):
Leave open: /WR (pin 39), PF7 / A15 (pin 48). Optional: LED + 1 kΩ from +5 V to PC5 (pin 16) — the reader blinks it while dumping, solid when done.
QFP-64 14×20: 19 pins on long sides, 13 on short
verify against VDD 58 / VSS 26 with a meter
